The implementation exceeds the declared API batch cap, violates its bounded-memory guarantee, and inconsistently accepts the forbidden quota boundary. All five existing tests pass despite these reproduced failures.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Size batches using API_BATCH_LIMIT — <worktree>/docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py:18-18
  Inputs exceeding 256 records produce batches that violate the documented API cap: 257 records yield one 257-record batch, while 1,000 yield sizes `[265, 265, 265, 205]`. These batches will be rejected. Use `API_BATCH_LIMIT` for both the slice width and stride, and test the maximum batch length rather than only batch counts.

- [P2] Stream batches instead of retaining the entire input — <worktree>/docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py:17-18
  For large iterables, `list(records)` materializes every record and the comprehension retains every output batch simultaneously, contradicting the stated one-batch memory bound. A tracemalloc probe with ten million repeated `None` records peaked at 162,424,336 bytes, versus the documented limit of 4 MB. Yield batches incrementally and update the tests to exercise incremental consumption.

- [P2] Enforce the strict reserve boundary consistently — <worktree>/docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-batcher/batcher.py:24-25
  Three 30% shares leave exactly the forbidden 10% reserve, but `[0.3, 0.3, 0.3]` returns `0.10000000000000009` and is accepted because of floating-point rounding; the equivalent `[0.9]` allocation is rejected. The equal-shares test explicitly requires this incorrect acceptance. Define quota precision using decimal or integer units, enforce the boundary at that precision, and require both representations of a 90% allocation to raise.
